title: Economic resources
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the three-way classification of natural, human and capital resources; they only mention resources in passing while covering price signals and international trade.

draft.title: Economic resources
card: Goods are things you can touch, such as bread or a bike. Services are things done for you, such as a haircut. Both are made using economic resources.
things that come from nature, such as land, water and minerals.
the work and skills of people.
things made to help produce other goods and services, such as tools, machines and buildings.
draft.remember: Goods and services are made from natural, human and capital resources.

a.q: Which of these is a capital resource for a bakery in Bendigo?
opts: An oven used to bake the bread
The wheat grown on a farm
The water from the local river
a.why: An oven is a machine made to help produce bread, so it is a capital resource. The wheat and water come from nature, so they are natural resources. The baker's skills are a human resource.
a.clue: Which one was made by people to help produce other things?

b.q: Mia runs a surf school in Torquay. Which of these is a human resource she uses?
opts: Her instructors' skill at teaching surfing
The beach where lessons are held
The shed that stores the wetsuits
b.why: Human resources are the work and skills of people, so the instructors' teaching skill is the human resource. The surfboards and the shed are capital resources, as they are made to help produce lessons. The beach comes from nature, so it is a natural resource.
b.clue: Look for the option about what people can do, not what they use.

a.best: An oven used to bake the bread

b.best: Her instructors' skill at teaching surfing
